scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Dancers wear towering head-dresses made of bison horns and peacock plumes to mimic the movements of the hunt, a tradition preserved by the Sing Marias of South Bastar.
This is Gaur Maria Dance. 20th century to present.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (RtNwAjTY22s)
Title card: Gaur Maria Dance · India · 20th century to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is a traditional folk form of the Sing Marias (also known as Tallaguda Marias) of South Bastar.
It is historically documented as a popular dance of the Madhya Pradesh region, specifically within the Bastar plateau which is now part of Chhattisgarh.
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed primarily for marriages, the dance is a celebration of joy and a tribute to the spirit of hunting.
It serves to depict hunting procedures and reinforce tribal identity through communal performance.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Men and women join in a gathering where men beat drums and toss their horned head-gears.
The dance depicts hunting procedures through movement.
As the tempo rises, the movements become more intense and 'wild,' involving the tossing of plumes and horns in synchronization with the drum beats.
Watch for Horn Tossing, Hunting Depiction.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (RtNwAjTY22s)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Performed in an open dancing ground; starts as a gathering and moves into a synchronized group display.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The primary instruments are drums played by the men.
The music is characterized by a rising tempo that dictates the energy of the dance.
Listen for the Drums, Cowrie shells (as idiophones), Brass fillets (visual/rhythmic).

The sound is dominated by the synchronized beating of drums by the male dancers. As the dance progresses, the tempo increases, creating a driving, hypnotic rhythm. The clattering of cowrie shells on the head-dresses adds a high-pitched percussive layer to the deep thrum of the drums.

images.description:
Gaur Maria dance 
This dance is performed by men and women of Bison Horn Maria tribe  of Bastar in Madhya Pradesh,This is basically performed on the occasion of marriages . It appears to be a hunt-dance with only the imitation of the frisking, jerking movements of the animals.
